\section[a lâmpada]{a lâmpada — a lamp; a light bulb}

\label{lesson:PT-C50-lampada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for a roof, then the Portuguese for a garden.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a lâmpada}
\textbf{a lâmpada} — \textquotedblleft{}a lamp; a light bulb\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{lâmpada} $\leftarrow$ Late Latin \emph{lampada}, \textquotedblleft{}torch, lamp\textquotedblright{} — a learned borrowing from Late Latin. EtymDB 2.1 traces it only to Old Portuguese \emph{lampada}; it derives Spanish \emph{lámpada} from Late Latin \emph{lampada}, from Latin \emph{lampas}.
\end{cousinweb}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o chão}
\textbf{o chão} — \textquotedblleft{}the floor, the ground\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{chão} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{planus}, \textquotedblleft{}flat, level\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1) — inherited. Latin \emph{pl-} became \emph{ch-}, and the lost \emph{-n-} left a nasal vowel.
\end{cousinweb}
